data.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?

result.keyword: What's the best password manager for a small team?
result.markdown:
For most small teams, I'd recommend **1Password** as the best overall choice. It's easy to use, has excellent shared-vault functionality, and makes managing employee access straightforward.

However, **Bitwarden** is arguably the better choice if keeping costs down is a priority.

Here are the three I'd shortlist.

## Best password managers for small teams

![1Password 8.12 - TidBITS](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/34HDvvYhqgd6AnMFmrlTm3hAXFxcbeGEwY_LB_XZ_XGVtrk4a2QxTEX-2LBZt2GGXhIIaKEolAWfkyjqt2bzeCs60tKyMvcGjArpm-vdyy1ZPxujq2f9_l2uItYJrXcwCcU9bPBSy8AGv_Ou2YF6Ce5xYeilxXBZ8f7ED4T1F4V2OwIPdBn46M8zBrxXTO4w?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. 1Password**

(Best overall)

- Excellent user experience
- Shared vaults with granular permissions
- Easy onboarding and employee offboarding
- Strong administrative controls

Teams Starter Pack: approximately US\$24.95/month for up to 10 users, billed annually.

[1Password business plans](https://1password.com/business)

---

![The best password managers in 2026 | Tom's Guide](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/NzVuMgIchg5mHs-Kr9143cu9YVcLD78U-cfqnnpzpdksR6kB5LPVR6OyqUe0J0PAWilFgVX5RafeZ-AzNa_G6WUPgI8J1U4oAahEfqnQQL2SaxhVwFg9jy1o1kVewXMyq40iQ1cCkpkzpsh_DQntfgs6e3PLRpQFbO3dRcV-HQGbTSkVwYxuDvCJM657Aw6_?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Bitwarden**

(Best value)

- Very competitive pricing
- Open-source software
- Shared collections for teams
- Audit logs and directory integrations

Teams: approximately US\$4/user/month, billed annually.

[Bitwarden business plans](https://bitwarden.com/business/)

---

![Keeper Security Logo PNG,  Vector (AI, EPS, CDR, PDF, SVG) - iconLogoVector](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/hjZLLtGaZjkKvsDiCoIrNA749yx3vMYIFoRmmV0blB-pAj7O30nu3RJOVVhVRwgAOkJUfJ3datZ7pfH1wp7yeplrEL3FQ-HNOpCzlVOW0OcMr1CFjIFAx50apRkdH6sYOH31WcP6gfXOxeAN8qubYhHhGYA5yXp1bc7wqtCxjN2WEQuyMALTG1Pwne14BXyG?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. Keeper**

- Good administrative controls
- Shared team folders
- Role-based access management
- Useful for businesses with stricter security requirements

Business Starter: approximately US\$2/user/month, billed annually, subject to eligibility.

[Keeper business plans](https://www.keepersecurity.com/business.html)

Pricing is indicative, in USD, and may vary by billing region and plan. [toolsandthrive.com](https://toolsandthrive.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.northvetted.ca](https://www.northvetted.ca/reviews/best-password-manager-canada?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.softwarecompare.net](https://www.softwarecompare.net/comparison/best-password-manager-for-business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## My recommendation

| Your situation | My choice |
|--------|--------|
| 3–10 employees | 1Password |
| 10–30 employees, budget-conscious | Bitwarden |
| Security-heavy business | Keeper |
| Non-technical employees | 1Password |
| Canadian data residency matters | 1Password or Keeper |


Since you're potentially operating in Quebec, I'd also consider where company credentials and related personal information are hosted. 1Password and Keeper offer Canadian data-region options. [toolsandthrive.com](https://toolsandthrive.com/best-password-manager-for-small-business/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.northvetted.ca](https://www.northvetted.ca/reviews/best-password-manager-canada?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.softwarecompare.net](https://www.softwarecompare.net/comparison/best-password-manager-for-business?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What I'd insist on, whichever you choose

- **Shared vaults\:** Share company credentials without sending passwords through Slack or email.
- **Individual accounts\:** Never share one master login among employees.
- **Access controls\:** Control who can see and edit each password.
- **Offboarding\:** Immediately revoke access when someone leaves.
- **2FA\:** Require two-factor authentication.
- **Audit logs\:** Know who accessed or changed credentials.

## One question to narrow it down

**How many people will need access?**
